# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 99 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_099_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 99

**1** The disciples said to him: "Your brothers and your mother are standing outside."

**2** He said to them: "Those here who do the will of my Father — these are my brothers and my mother.

**3** They are the ones who will enter the kingdom of my Father."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Standing outside"** — EMET/LOGOS preferred: the Coptic *aheratou ebol* = standing outside. PNEUMA's "waiting outside" adds an expectation that is not in the text.

**"My Father"** — used twice, marking both the criterion (will of my Father) and the destination (kingdom of my Father). The familial language is sustained throughout.

**Theological Note:** Thomas's version adds the eschatological promise: "will enter the kingdom of my Father." This is Thomas's distinctive contribution — the biological family is "outside," both physically and spiritually, while those who do the Father's will are both family and kingdom-entrants.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Mark 3:31-35; Matt 12:46-50; Luke 8:19-21. All versions have the redefinition of family; only Thomas adds the kingdom-entry promise.
